headline: Xi lands. Trump meets him at the plane.
summary: Xi Jinping landed at Joint Base Andrews Wednesday evening, his first state visit in over a decade, and Trump met him at the plane. Presidents usually wait at the White House; the last airport welcomes went to popes. Three days follow: a state dinner Thursday with Elon Musk and Jensen Huang, then tea and the National Archives on Friday.

cover_question.q: Why go to the airport for him?

cover_answer: To honor him. Trump got no such welcome in China in May.
table_question: Does a bigger welcome make a guest owe you something?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: China's leader, Xi Jinping, flew to Washington today, and the president went to the airport to meet him at the plane. Usually a president waits at home for the visitor to come to the door. It is like walking to the end of the street to meet a friend instead of waiting on the porch. A big welcome, and the grown-ups are doing the talking.
5-7.why: Meeting a friend at the end of the street is a thing they've done. Two people and a plane.
5-7.why_long: Countries are too big for a five-year-old to picture, so the script shrinks it to two people, a plane and a porch, a scene they know. One vivid detail, the walk out to meet a friend, stands in for the whole visit. Expect "is China our friend?" The presidents say so; the countries argue plenty.

8-12.script: In May Trump got a red carpet and 300 flag-waving kids in China, but Xi did not come to the airport. Now it is China's turn, and Trump went one further: he met Xi on the tarmac, a welcome lately saved for popes. The host who meets you at the car, not the door. AP says expectations for a deal are low.
8-12.why: May's welcome, this week's answer. The host at the car is the rule.
8-12.why_long: This age tracks fairness and turn-taking, so the script builds it as one: Trump's May welcome, then Xi's turn, then Trump going one better. The host meeting you at the car is a rule they understand without being told what it means. Expect "will they agree on anything?" AP says not much this week, and that is allowed.

13-17.script: Sen. Roger Wicker, a Republican, says Trump should not have invited a man he calls a brutal dictator. Is a warm welcome a tool or a gift? Second: Xi skipped the airport when Trump landed in Beijing, and now Trump has out-hosted him. Does that buy anything?
13-17.why: Both true: the welcome, and Wicker's "dictator". Ask what a welcome is for. They can hold both and are testing whether you will.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold both the red carpet and Wicker's speech, and the script gives them nothing else, so they have to decide what a welcome is for. Ask whether they would shake the hand, and argue it straight; they are testing whether you will. Expect "so is this just for show?" AP says a deal is unlikely, and the show may be the point.

5-7.a: The presidents say they're friends. The countries argue a lot, and this week they're talking.

8-12.q: Why go to the airport for him?
8-12.a: To honor him. Trump got no such greeting in China in May.
AP says expectations are low. The big items: trade, AI chips, Taiwan.

13-17.q: Why be nice to a dictator?
13-17.a: White House: he'll deal with anyone for US interests. Wicker objects.
AP says a breakthrough is unlikely; the aim is a steady relationship.
